title: ExecutionProfile
description:
Response body of POST /v1/route (HTTP 200). The planning-time decision, stamped IMMUTABLY into story frontmatter.

INVARIANT 2 (planning-time immutability): the profile chosen for an execution attempt is frozen. A worker may not re-choose its model mid-attempt; re-routing requires a NEW attempt with a new call to /v1/route.

INVARIANT 1 (three independent axes): harness, model_profile and placement_policy are three separate fields on purpose. No consumer may collapse two of them into one, and nothing here names a physical model or an endpoint - resolving a profile onto physical compute is /v1/place's job, and substituting a different model is never legitimate (invariant 3).

VOCABULARY: harness, model_profile and placement_policy are closed enums taken verbatim from ConfigMap ai/agent-router-catalog, catalog document version 1.1.0, schema_version 1. They are not restated from memory. See README 'Vocabulary coupling' for the change protocol that keeps this file and the catalog in step.

harness.description: Which autonomous coding harness runs the work.

model_profile.description: Logical model/capability profile. The only model-ish name BMAD stamps; the physical model behind it moves by catalog PR underneath a stable profile name.

effort.description: Reasoning-effort tier for the harness session.

cost_class.description:
How THIS ATTEMPT will be paid for. Invariant 4 is written per-attempt ("Billable use is explicit, per-attempt, and recorded"), so this is a property of the attempt, not a copy of the catalog field.

`free` - local GPU, or a free vendor tier.
`subscription` - a seat the operator already pays for (invariant 10: a subscription is NOT an API key, and nothing here authorises centralising an OAuth token or introducing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
`metered` - billable per-token spend. DEFAULT-DENY (invariant 4).

It normally equals the selected profile's catalog cost_class, and differs exactly when the profile's usual payment path is unavailable and a billable one exists for the same profile - a subscription pool exhausted for the window, say. That case is the reason the distinction matters: it is where an unguarded router would quietly start spending money.

entitlement_pool.description:
WHICH funding source backs this attempt. `cost_class` says what the attempt costs; this says where that money comes from. They are different questions and neither is derivable from the other.

null is a legitimate value, not a gap: local execution draws on no entitlement pool, because the GPU is already paid for.

WHY A CONSUMER NEEDS IT. The dispatcher has to place the attempt in the correct, ISOLATED provider credential environment before it starts, and the only alternatives to being told are guesses: infer the provider from the harness (wrong - `claude` runs against Anthropic Max on one attempt and against MiniMax on another), or infer it from the credential the environment happens to hold (wrong, and dangerous - see below). Naming the pool removes both guesses.

BILLING CLASS AND CREDENTIAL TYPE ARE INDEPENDENT AXES (owner ruling R16). A pool's economics are a fact about the ENTITLEMENT; the credential is a fact about the SHAPE of the secret used to reach it. NEITHER IMPLIES THE OTHER. Concretely: MiniMax's Max Token Plan is a FIXED MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION reached with a provider-issued, API-KEY-SHAPED credential. `looks like an API key, therefore cost_class: metered` is WRONG BY CONSTRUCTION - a consumer that reasons that way bills a flat subscription as per-token spend and refuses work the operator has already paid for. The heuristic is embedded in tooling elsewhere in this estate, so it is contradicted here explicitly rather than left to be re-derived.

This schema deliberately does NOT constrain cost_class against entitlement_pool. Encoding a pool-to-cost mapping here would be the same mistake in a different place: deriving economics from a name this contract happens to enumerate, rather than from the catalog entry that declares them. The catalog is authoritative (`entitlement_pools`, four declared attributes per pool), and this being a MUST the schema cannot check is recorded in the README's open items.

INVARIANT 4. Exhausting a pool NEVER promotes to billable spend: every seeded pool declares `spillover: none`, so an exhausted pool simply stops being a candidate and routing falls back to another approved pool, to free, or to local. In particular MiniMax Token Plan exhaustion must never spill into MiniMax pay-as-you-go - those are two credential classes for two entitlements, and holding one grants nothing about the other. A metered path requires all three of a separately provisioned metered credential, `allow_metered` intent, and independent metered-spend authorization held by the caller.

placement_policy.description: Which placement policy /v1/place must resolve this attempt under. Stamped at planning time so that dispatch-time placement cannot silently widen the set of compute the attempt may land on. It is inert while the selected profile is vendor-hosted (placement_required false) and binds only if the attempt runs on local compute.

placement_required.description:
Does this attempt need a physical placement decision before it can be dispatched?

true - a LOCAL profile. The model is served through agentgateway on a specific GPU, so the client MUST call /v1/place with the stamped model_profile and placement_policy, and MUST send the returned x-placement header. Dispatching without placing means gateway-side selection, which may be exactly the compute the stamped policy excluded.
false - a VENDOR profile, resolved by the harness itself (the catalog records these as resolved_by: harness). There is no placement to make: the traffic never touches agentgateway, and calling /v1/place for it would be a meaningless round trip. Launch the harness directly.

WHY IT IS A FIELD RATHER THAN SOMETHING THE CLIENT WORKS OUT: without it a client has to carry its own copy of which profiles are local - either by duplicating catalog knowledge that is deliberately not published in this contract, or by inferring from the `local-` name prefix, which is a naming convention and not a guarantee. Both go stale the moment the catalog moves, and both fail silently. The router already knows the answer; it says so.

It equals `hosting: local` for the SELECTED profile in the loaded catalog. That equality is a MUST on the router which this schema cannot check, because model/profile hosting is catalog data and this contract deliberately does not enumerate it (README 'Vocabulary coupling').

fallbacks.description:
Ordered alternatives, most preferred first, for use when the primary choice cannot start AT ALL (e.g. the harness pool is exhausted). Empty array is legal and means 'no fallback: fail the attempt instead'.

A fallback is a NEW ATTEMPT, not a mid-attempt swap (invariant 2). Every entry obeys the same rules as the primary: no metered entry may appear unless the request set allow_metered: true, and the harness enum is equally closed.

metered.description:
True only when this attempt is authorized to spend billable API budget. INVARIANT 4 - metered API is default-deny: absence of subscription or local capacity never silently promotes to billable API. True here requires allow_metered: true on the /v1/route request; the router refuses otherwise (see metered_denied).

allow_metered: true IS NOT ITSELF AUTHORIZATION. It expresses INTENT - the caller is asking for a billable option to be considered - and the router grants it only if the AUTHENTICATED CALLER independently holds authority to approve metered spend. The ordinary automation principal (the BMAD dispatcher and every machine caller like it) does NOT hold that authority, and a request from one carrying allow_metered: true is refused 403 metered_authorization_required rather than served. A boolean a client can set for itself is a request, not a control.

rationale.description: One human-readable paragraph citing the deciding signals (blast radius, ambiguity, tags, capacity, cost). This is read by a human reviewing a stamped story months later; 'policy said so' is not a rationale.

catalog_document_version.description: Additive, optional. The catalog's own semver `version` field (e.g. "1.0.0"), carried so a stale-catalog message can name a human-meaningful version rather than only a digest. Never a substitute for catalog_version in an equality check.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339. After this instant the decision is stale and MUST be recomputed by calling /v1/route again rather than dispatched. Expiry exists because the inputs (pool temperature, capacity, catalog) move; it is not a cache TTL for the response body.

allOf.description: INVARIANT 4, mechanically: `metered` is true exactly when the selected cost_class is metered. A profile that claims cost_class=metered with metered=false would spend money without authorization; the reverse would record an authorization that bought nothing.

The metered_denied note is only meaningful on a substituted, non-metered result: it says 'the best option was withheld and this is the best remaining one'. It can never accompany a profile that is itself metered.

harness.description:
INVARIANT 16 - the harness axis accepts claude|codex|devin ONLY. `local-agent` exists in the catalog as a RESERVED, supported:false / selectable:false placeholder so the axis is future-proof, and the catalog states router_behaviour: refuse-to-emit. A router that emits it is wrong and must refuse loudly rather than degrade.

llama.cpp, vLLM and llama-swap are INFERENCE RUNTIME, not autonomous coding harnesses, and no harness may be adopted merely to fill an architectural slot. Making `local-agent` selectable requires its own story evaluating a specific harness; no story in EPIC-035 does that.

The redundant `not` clause is deliberate belt-and-braces: it keeps the refusal true even if somebody later widens the enum without reading this description.
harness.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.1.0 harnesses table, entries with selectable: true.

model_profile.description:
Profile names read verbatim from catalog v1.1.0.

SEVEN ARE SELECTABLE; `minimax/strong` IS NOT. It is declared in catalog 1.1.0 with selectable: false and a blocked_by list, so the router must not emit it today. It is in this enum anyway, exactly as the placement enum carries `status: planned` placement names: the name is frozen now so the catalog and this contract land together, and flipping it to selectable is then a catalog change alone. Excluding it would mean a contract PR had to accompany that flip, which is the catalog-versus-contract drift window the 404 taxonomy exists to describe. It is NOT `local-agent`: that one is refuse-to-emit permanently by invariant 16 and is excluded from the harness enum on purpose. Whether a profile is selectable today is catalog state, and no schema here can check it.

INVARIANT 12 - `local-unrestricted` is an ALIGNMENT property, not a quality tier: it is a weaker model than local-code-standard in every respect except refusal behaviour. Its catalog forbidden_for list (security, iam, secrets, prod-iac, destructive-tools) is a HARD EXCLUSION, not a score or a tie-break: a /v1/route request carrying any of those tags must never be auto-selected onto it, however well it otherwise fits. An operator may still choose it explicitly and own that choice.
model_profile.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.1.0 profiles table.

entitlement_pool.description:
Funding-source names read verbatim from catalog v1.1.0 `entitlement_pools`. Each pool declares four attributes there - provider, cost_class, credential_class and spillover - so a consumer never infers one from another.

The seeded set makes the independence of billing and credential concrete: `anthropic-max` and `minimax-max` are both subscriptions with completely different credential shapes (a signed-in subscription session versus a provider-issued API key), and `devin-free` is free rather than a subscription at all - which is why this is an ENTITLEMENT pool and not a subscription pool. A future explicitly-authorized pay-as-you-go source would be a fifth entry with `cost_class: metered`, and adding it is an additive minor bump here plus a catalog PR; no such pool exists.
entitlement_pool.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.1.0 entitlement_pools table.

placement_policy.description: Policy names read verbatim from catalog v1.1.0 policies.placement_policy. `prefer-warm-local` is the catalog default applied when a caller names none. `edge-only` has resolves_today: false - every placement it names is status: planned - so /v1/place answers it with an explicit unavailable result rather than falling through to the cluster.
placement_policy.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.1.0 policies.placement_policy table.

catalog_version.description:
Content digest of the catalog this decision was computed against: sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the rendered catalog document (ConfigMap ai/agent-router-catalog, key catalog.yaml) exactly as mounted, before any parsing. Computed by the router at load time; never written by hand and never equal to the catalog's semver `version` field.

A caller may echo this value back on a later request to assert it is still planning against the same catalog; a mismatch is answered with 409 catalog_version_stale rather than silently served.

entitlement_pool.description: Which funding source would back this alternative. Carried per entry, and required, for the same reason the primary carries it: the economics of EVERY candidate must be auditable BEFORE anything runs, not discovered when a fallback is taken. A fallback routinely crosses funding sources - a local attempt falling back to a subscription pool is the ordinary shape - and a client that has just failed over is the last one that should be inferring which credential environment to use.

placement_required.description: Same meaning as on the profile itself, for this alternative: true means the client calls /v1/place before dispatching it, false means it launches the harness directly. Carried per entry because a fallback can cross the local/vendor line - a local primary falling back to a vendor profile is the ordinary case - and a client that has just failed over is exactly the client that should not be guessing.

fallback.description: One alternative attempt: the axes a fallback may change, plus whether it needs placing. It deliberately cannot carry an effort tier or a placement policy - those stay as stamped, so a fallback cannot quietly widen the attempt's blast radius.

code.description: Same machine-readable code as the 409 error of the same name. One condition, two carriers: this in-band note when a non-metered substitute exists, and a 409 error envelope when none does. A caller distinguishes them by whether it received a profile at all.

message.description: Human-readable explanation naming what was withheld and why.

obligation.description: The caller's obligation. Proceeding with the returned non-metered profile is legitimate and is the expected path. The alternative is a NEW /v1/route call carrying allow_metered: true, which is a per-attempt human authorization decision - never an automatic retry. A client that retries with allow_metered: true on its own has defeated invariant 4.

withheld.description:
The metered option the router would have returned had the request carried allow_metered: true, AND had the caller held authority to approve it. Recorded so the human authorizing the spend can see exactly what they are authorizing.

It deliberately carries no entitlement_pool. A withheld option is one that was NOT funded from anywhere: the whole content of the refusal is that no authorized funding source existed for it. Naming a pool here would suggest the router had picked one, which is the opposite of what happened.

metered_denied.description: INVARIANT 4 refusal note. Present on a 200 response when the best option was metered, the request did not set allow_metered: true, and a non-metered option existed; the profile carried alongside it IS that non-metered option. When no non-metered option exists the router returns 409 metered_denied with no profile instead - it never returns the metered choice with a warning attached.
